question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The correct answer is D, "Association, an". The blank falls between an independent clause — "At the turn of the twentieth century, Callie House helped lead the National Ex-Slave Mutual Relief, Bounty and Pension Association" — and a nonrestrictive appositive that renames the organization: "an organization that enrolled tens of thousands of formerly enslaved people in a campaign for federal pensions." Standard English sets off such an appositive with a comma, which D supplies. A period (A) makes the appositive a sentence fragment, since "An organization that enrolled … opposition" has no main verb. A semicolon (B) must join two independent clauses, but the appositive is not independent. No punctuation (C) fuses the appositive to the head noun in a run-on.

_meta.anchor: Callie House — National Ex-Slave Mutual Relief, Bounty and Pension Association; nonrestrictive appositive comma
